about.title: Irwindale Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Irwindale's mix of industrial operations, quarries, and warehouse distribution centers means residents and workers regularly interact with heavy equipment, tools, packaging materials, and consumer goods moving through the area. When one of these products fails because of a flaw in how it was designed, built, or labeled, the resulting injury can be severe and disrupt a person's ability to work or care for their family. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a claim without proving the manufacturer was careless — the defect and the harm it caused are usually enough. LawProactive is a free service that connects Irwindale residents with an independent personal injury attorney familiar with these claims. The attorney can review what happened, help identify which companies in the supply chain may share responsibility, and explain next steps. There's no fee unless the attorney recovers compensation for you, and reaching out costs nothing.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Defective Product

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Under California law, you often don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — showing the product was defective and caused your injury may be enough.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which an attorney can help sort out based on how the product moved through the supply chain.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: An attorney can advise you early on how to keep the product intact and unaltered, since it often serves as key evidence in a defect claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California generally allows strict liability claims for defective products, meaning you typically just need to show the product was flawed and that flaw caused your injury. An independent attorney can review your situation and explain how this applies to your case.

items.question: I was hurt by equipment at a distribution facility near I-605 in Irwindale — does that change anything?
items.answer: Industrial and warehouse injuries can sometimes involve both workplace claims and separate product liability claims against the equipment maker. An attorney can look at the specifics of your incident and help determine which paths apply.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, without repairing or discarding it. The product itself is often central evidence, and an attorney can advise you on safely preserving it.
